item.title: Trump’s Border Czar Says ‘Small’ Security Force Will Remain In Minnesota After Enforcement Drawdown
item.description: By BEN FINLEY Associated Press WASHINGTON (AP) — White House border czar Tom Homan said Sunday that more than 1,000 immigration agents have left Minnesota’s Twin Cities area and hundreds more will depart in the days ahead as part of the Trump administration’s drawdown of its immigration enforcement surge. item.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Sparks Fires At Russian Black Sea Port Ahead Of US-Brokered Peace Talks
item.description: By The Associated Press A Ukrainian drone strike ignited fires at one of Russia’s Black Sea ports, officials said Sunday, ahead of fresh talks aimed at ending the nearly 4-year-old war. Two people were wounded in the attack on the port of Taman in the Krasnodar region, which damaged an oil storage tank, warehouse and terminals, according to regional Gov. Veniamin Kondratyev. item.title: Border Drone Warning
item.description: A Texas congressman is concerned about the increasing use of drones by Mexican cartels. Democrat Henry Cuellar says this has become a huge problem in South Texas as the smugglers leverage technology to spy on Border Patrol. Meanwhile, Senators want a classified briefing so the Trump administration can explain reports that air space over El Paso was shut down last week so Border Patrol could use laser technology to shoot down a drone.

item.title: School Choice Expansion
item.description: More than 100-thousand Texas families have signed up for a new private school voucher program. Governor Greg Abbott says that demand is so strong that he would like to see it expanded. The program gives parents greater flexibility in choosing the best education for their child. Those selected in a lottery will be able to pull their kid from public school and use their tax dollars to send them to a private school.

item.title: ICE Center Debate
item.description: The San Antonio City Council has ordered staff to find ways to push back against a new ICE detention center, but not everybody is on board. item.title: Trucking Comment Blasted
item.description: Democratic Senate Candidate Jasmine Crockett is facing pushback from some in the trucking industry. The congresswoman suggested that truck drivers should not have to be required to speak English in order to get a commercial license. She argues that you can rent a car without passing a language test. Jeffery Burkhardt with the Commercial Vehicle Training Association says that’s insulting. He points out that the rules of the road are different for those driving 80-thousand pound vehicles.
